_source: Every job on this board was written for this board. The QUESTIONS are the exception to nothing: each one is answered by a sentence that is already published on the page the marker sits on, and each was read off that page before it was written here rather than remembered. Where a question asks for a person's name it is a name our own page already credits -- Barad, Oldaker, Schaber, Thornburg, Lee and Duffy -- because a quiz that made somebody guess at an attribution would be teaching the opposite of the habit this street kept.
_codes: One word, A-Z, typed case-insensitively with spaces and punctuation ignored. A word rather than a random string because a word can be said out loud, remembered across a walk to another room, and typed by somebody who finds typing expensive. These are not secrets and the board does not pretend they are: the code is printed in the room's own markup, on a public page, and anybody who wants to read the source can have the lot. The board holds a checksum instead of the plain word purely so that View Source on ONE page is not a spoiler sheet for every room. That is a courtesy, not a lock, and make-guild.py says so where it computes it.
_no_score: There is no tally here, no percentage, no streak, no rank you climb and nothing that expires. The board stamps a job when you hand its code in and that is the whole of the bookkeeping. This is the pebbling cabinet's refusal arriving in the one room on the street most likely to talk itself out of it -- a job board is EXACTLY the shape of thing that grows a score, and a score beside a Disabled people's walking tour would quietly turn a wander into a workload. make-guild.py refuses the vocabulary.
_class: The difficulty class is HOW FAR YOU WALK, not how clever you are. I is on the street, II is through a door off a room, III is out past the treeline. Nothing about the class says anything about the person doing it, which is the whole reason it is defined by geography and enumerated in the tool rather than typed per job.

quests.title: Read the street before you walk it
quests.posted: Somebody has chalked a mark on the kerb outside the guild. Go and look at it. This is the shortest job on the board and it exists so that the first one you ever do is one you cannot get wrong.
quests.target: a chalk mark on the kerb
hints: It is on the front page, not behind any door.
Go to the very bottom of the street, past the shopfronts and past the signpost, to where the pavement is.
Right at the foot of the street, down on the pavement below the signpost.

quests.title: Whose records are on that dancefloor
quests.posted: There is a sequin on the floor of the Pink Pony Club. Pick it up, and while you are down there settle an argument about who owns the music in that room.

ask.question: The room says it out loud near the jukebox: how much of the music in here is hosted by us? One word.
ask.why: Every player in that room is a press-to-play facade. Nothing is fetched from YouTube until you press, nothing is copied onto this site, and the room says so rather than leaving you to assume it.

The sentence is about who the music belongs to as well as where it lives.

It is behind the first shopfront on the street.
Look at the floor rather than at the jukebox.
Down on the dancefloor at the very bottom of the room, below the jukebox.
quests.learned: Press-to-play is the mechanism behind that claim, and it is checkable: open a network panel, load the room, and count the requests to YouTube. There are none until you press.

quests.title: A rhinestone off the vestments
quests.posted: A rhinestone has come off something in the Rhinestone Vatican and is lying on the floor of one of the arches. It is a subroom behind the dancefloor, so you will have to go through the Pink Pony Club to reach it.

On the chapel floor at the foot of the room, below the last arch.

quests.title: Read the door policy
quests.posted: There is a safety pin stuck through the paste-up wall at Club Chronic. Before it will come loose you have to have read what is pinned next to it, because that room makes a promise most clubs do not.

ask.question: This club names one thing it will never do, because it can put somebody on the floor. One word, and it is a kind of light.
ask.why: A room whose argument is come in as you are cannot have a light in it that causes seizures. The club has no ambient layer at any dial setting, and it says so on its own door policy so that nobody finishes the room later by adding one.
hints: It is on the door policy rather than in the music.
It is the one obvious effect a punk club has, and the one this club refuses.
Nothing plays until you press play, and nothing in here does the other thing.
It is a shopfront on the street, not behind a door.
It is the punk one, with the paste-up wall and the rack of records.
On the floor at the very bottom of the club, below the rack.
quests.learned: That room also says out loud that a loud room is an access barrier. A page celebrating a scene built out of volume, crowding and stairs, which never names who cannot get in, is doing the inspiration thing this organisation exists to refuse.

quests.title: One staple off the table

quests.title: How loud is the arcade
quests.posted: Somebody has dropped a token on the carpet in the arcade. Pick it up, and answer the thing the foyer says about itself that no real arcade could.

quests.title: Public domain everywhere

A site that serves everybody cannot publish a whole poem on a technicality that holds in one country.

quests.title: The two habits that survived
quests.posted: There is a colophon mark at the foot of the liner notes. This street dropped most of the care its sibling sites run on and kept exactly two things. Name the one that is not contrast.

ask.question: Two habits survived onto this street. One is contrast. What is the other? One word.
ask.why: It is a licence rather than a house style, it is the cheapest thing on the page, and it is the only one of our habits whose absence is a legal problem rather than an aesthetic one. So the credits got louder instead of going away.
hints: It is the thing this whole page is.
It is a licence rather than a house style.
Eleven letters, and it begins with an A.
It is one of the pages linked from the pavement at the foot of the street.

At the very bottom of the page, below the last credit.
quests.learned: Contrast survived for a reason that is not the obvious one. This is a Disabled people's organisation, and a glitter-maximalist site that excluded the people it is for would be a self-own of exactly the kind we exist to name. The fix was never to tone it down — it was the dial.

_where: EVERY MARKER IS ON THE FLOOR OF ITS ROOM, which on a web page means the bottom of it, and the guild says so out loud. Scattering them at a different depth in every room would have been more like a hunt and would have made finding one a test of eyesight and of a mouse -- on a Disabled people's site, where the hunt is meant to be the walk between rooms rather than the search within one. So the hints name the ROOM, the class says how far the walk is, and the last hint says where on the floor. What is never the same twice is the marker itself: one drawing per room, in that room's own colours, refused by make-guild.py if a room has none.
